# A component built at run time gives back what it kept when it is
# destroyed, on each platform placement writes C for: its record's destroy
# drops each field it kept -- a string, a list and its elements -- and then
# the record, a box kept like any other block (ir.Func.Frees). It gave back
# nothing, so each row a rebuilt list made grew the runtime's kept set by
# its prop, its vars and, on win32, the record itself. The test counts the
# kept blocks through the runtime's sngl_kept_blocks. Go collects what it
# allocates, so the program is C's alone.

[!gtk4] skip 'gtk4 needs its development libraries to build'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import c "sngl:x/c"
import macro "sngl:macro"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

c.link(include="sngl.h")

// How many blocks the runtime keeps: what every holder holds.
#[macro.cnative("sngl_kept_blocks")]
func keptBlocks() int

component row(label string) ui.node {
    var note = "row {label}"
    var tags list[string] = ["a {label}", "b {label}"]

    ui.text(value="{note} {tags.length()}")
}

component rows ui.node {
    var round = 0
    var labels list[string] = ["r0a", "r0b", "r0c"]

    ui.vbox {
        ui.button #next(text="next", @click {
            round += 1
            labels = ["r{round}a", "r{round}b", "r{round}c"]
        })
        for var l = labels {
            row(label=l)
        }
    }
}

func testARebuiltListKeepsNoMore(t test.Test, r rows) {
    r.next.click()
    var before = keptBlocks()
    r.next.click()
    r.next.click()
    t.assert(keptBlocks() == before)
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    rows
}
